frame.provenance: ENGINE-BACKED — source_frame_axis (7 coded frame axes, rank-1 value per axis per source).

Matthew.evidence: 'an angel of the Lord, descending from heaven' announces 'he has been raised' — the claim is grounded in angelic disclosure
'fear and great joy'; guards 'became like dead men'; luminous imagery ('like lightning', 'white as snow') — awe-saturated register
the ultimate irrupts into the world — angel descends, stone rolled back, empty tomb 'manifested' to the women as sign
narrated as event-report: dawn, earthquake, stone, empty place — presented as what happened, not as allegory
'suddenly there was a great earthquake, FOR an angel of the Lord... came and rolled back the stone' — event explained by agent-cause
'an angel of the Lord, descending from heaven' — a personal transcendent order breaks in with earthquake, lightning-appearance
'he has been raised' — resurrection as the decisive saving event the passage is oriented to proclaim

Mark.evidence: A 'young man dressed in a white robe' (angelophany) announces 'He has been raised' — the claim is grounded in supernatural disclosure, not observation.
'terror and amazement had seized them, and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid' — awe/numinous dread frames the narration; 'sacred and imperishable proclamation.'
The ultimate breaks into the world as event — angelic appearance, stone rolled away, promised christophany in Galilee ('there you will see him').
The crucifixion (apparent defeat) is re-narrated as vindication ('who was crucified. He has been raised'), integrating scandal into a redemptive whole.
Empty tomb + angelic interpretation → best-explanation inference to resurrection: 'you are looking for Jesus... He has been raised; he is not here. Look, there is the place they laid him.'
The reality asserted is a personal agent (Jesus of Nazareth) raised by divine passive ('he has been raised'), presupposing a transcendent personal God who acts.
Intermediate Ending: 'the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation'; the resurrection secures deliverance from death.

Luke.evidence: the women 'told all this to the eleven and to all the rest' — the text's mode of knowing is eyewitness report passed on
'terrified and bowed their faces to the ground'; Peter 'amazed at what had happened' — the narrator holds the object in awe
the resurrected one and the dazzling messengers appear within the world (tomb, dawn, spices) — the transcendent shows itself in ordinary space
the empty tomb + remembered prophecy + angelic word are woven into a single coherent vindication narrative that repairs the scandal of the cross
'Remember how he told you, while he was still in Galilee...' 'Then they remembered his words' — the empty tomb is read by recalling and interpreting prior prophecy
'the Son of Man must be handed over... and on the third day rise again' — reality is populated by named agents (Jesus, the Son of Man, the messengers) who act
'Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here but has risen' — the orienting end is God's vindicating deliverance from death

John.evidence: First-person eyewitness reports: Mary 'saw that the stone had been removed'; the beloved disciple 'saw and believed'; narrative of what witnesses observed at the tomb.
'the Lord', 'the disciple whom Jesus loved', angelic figures in white, solemn narration of the resurrection — the object is treated as holy.
The divine breaks into the world through the empty tomb, angelic appearance, and the risen Lord's presence — ultimate reality manifests within ordinary space (a garden tomb at dawn).
Narrative integrates confusion, grief, and scripture-not-yet-understood into a coherent redemptive event; loss ('they have taken away my Lord') is being repaired into recognition and belief.
The beloved disciple 'saw and believed' — inference to the best explanation from the arrangement of grave-cloths (empty tomb + orderly wrappings → resurrection, not theft).
'the Lord'; angels in white; a personal risen Jesus who transcends death yet remains agentive; God as personal actor implied through resurrection.
Resurrection of Jesus as the vindication that grounds salvation for believers; 'he must rise from the dead' frames a redemptive necessity.

frame.note: The radar's story is agreement vs divergence: all four share evaluative-stance=reverent and ground-world-relation=manifestation; they SPLIT on epistemic-warrant (revelation: Matthew/Mark; testimony: Luke/John — the ¶39 axis) and on ontological-commitment (Luke=personal-agentive vs the others' transcendent-personal). There is no 'material' weight in the coded data.
